name: SC-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: No polling or expert ratings available
model.rationale: Clyburn, a longtime incumbent with a big cash advantage, runs in a district that leans Democratic by double digits, and markets price his reelection at near certainty. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict the fundamentals, the seat stays Safe Democratic.
model.watch: An unexpectedly strong Republican fundraising push or redistricting changes could narrow what is otherwise a safely Democratic seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South Carolina's 6th District, anchored in Columbia and Charleston's more Democratic areas, has reelected Jim Clyburn repeatedly and leans Democratic by about 13 points on the partisan vote index. Clyburn, the longest-serving Black member of Congress and a former House Majority Whip, is running again and holds a clear financial edge, with more than $1.2 million raised and $1.6 million on hand. Republican challenger John Peterson has reported little fundraising activity.

No public general-election polls or expert race ratings are available for this contest, so the outlook rests on fundamentals. Prediction markets put Clyburn's chances at roughly 96 percent, consistent with the district's lean and his incumbency. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of polling rather than any sign of a competitive race.
